approach: Root cause: reading acceptance (`refusing_check`, crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of `step!` checks and none compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria. No rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it, so a reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` is accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k). Fix it at that gate with `check_request_parts`, placed last so every existing refusal keeps its refusing check. A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` line parts, inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences, and `-`/`*`/`N.` bullets after an `Acceptance:` line (a Bullet kind only, never counted twice). It skips quoted-evidence lines of generated root-cause requests, including the title line `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: ...`. Coverage uses DISTINCTIVE stems so sibling parts cannot cover each other. Revision, round 4 findings: (1) a negation phrase is ignored for a part whose own text contains it, so 'status lists skipped checks' covers '(2) Report skipped checks in status'; the everyday words skipped, omitted and excluded cancel a criterion only when it cites the part's marker; work-state phrases (deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of) and job-scope phrases still cancel; the error names every ignored criterion and the phrase that caused it; new corpus cases pin both sides. (2) The title line is skipped like 'Cause:'; a corpus case with '(1) .. (2) ..' in the cause pins it. (3) A line after `Acceptance:` is a Bullet only and never an Enumerated part; a parser test pins it. (4) The filler and stop lists apply to the bare word and to its singular stem, 'passes'/'passed' are listed, and `part_stems_worked_examples` pins 'A test fails without the change and passes with it'. Enforced by code only; no prompt, config or record is edited.

decisions.choice: 1. Add a new parser `request_parts(text) -> Vec<RequestPart {marker, kind, text, span}>` in topics.rs (kind = Enumerated or Bullet); leave `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet` unchanged. Skip quoted-evidence lines: those starting 'Introspection ', 'Cause:', 'Failure class:', 'Priority:' or 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:', and those holding 'prevention it proposed:'. Read inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences only from the remaining non-bullet lines, only when every marker is followed by text with a significant stem, and end the last part at the first '. ' or line end.
decisions.reason: `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs:276, plan_entry 411) and is called by steward.rs:587/1566/1582/1658, hestia.rs:1781 and code_health.rs:1348, and the corpus pins its bullet counts (refusal_corpus.rs:2788-2794). Generated root-cause requests quote the cause on the title line (hestia.rs:1050-1053: 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: {first 100 chars of cause_text}'), on 'Cause:' (1027), and each proposal on 'Introspection {id} (job {job}); prevention it proposed: ...' (1041). An enumeration in any of them must not become required parts, because the root-cause default lets the reader fix the cause another way (hestia.rs:1017-1022). Finding 2: the title is a truncated copy of the cause, so it is skipped too; terms.rs:70 already treats that prefix as a generated-request marker, so the prefix is a stable key.

rejected.option: Extend `is_bullet` to read `N)` and `(a)` lines
rejected.why: Moves plan acceptance of every queued request and the pinned bullet counts.

rejected.option: Read inline sequences from the whole request
rejected.why: A quoted proposal or the cause title with text after each marker would be required as parts.

rejected.option: Skip any line whose text after the colon is a prefix of the 'Cause:' line
rejected.why: More logic than a fixed prefix, and no extra lines are caught.

decisions.reason: The new step runs only when every other check passes, so each existing Refuse case keeps its refusing check; `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line (refusal_corpus.rs:2927) and still works. Only Accept cases with explicit parts can change.

rejected.option: Place it early, after `check_criteria_evidence`
rejected.why: It would pre-empt `check_outcome_state` in the delivery cases that carry `2)` and `(a)` parts (refusal_corpus.rs:936-949).

decisions.choice: 3. Kinds, stated exactly. Enumerated: line-start `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` and inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences, found on lines BEFORE the `Acceptance:` heading (and on `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` lines after it). Bullet: a line that starts `-`, `*` or `N.` AFTER a line equal to `Acceptance:` (case-insensitive). A line after the heading in a bullet form is a Bullet only: it is never also scanned as an Enumerated part, and its inline text is not scanned for `(1)..(2)` sequences, so no line is counted twice and no part gets both needs. `N.` lines before the heading are Enumerated. Parser unit test `request_parts_numbered_line_after_acceptance_is_a_bullet_only` uses the steward.rs:1579 shape ('Acceptance:' then '1. It parses') and asserts one Bullet and no Enumerated part.
decisions.reason: Finding 3. The failure class is a dropped enumerated part such as (3); acceptance bullets are the second introspection's proposal. The two kinds need different numbers of matching stems (2 and 1), so each line needs exactly one kind. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests (reading.rs:2638, 2753, 2951; drain.rs:3988, 4067, 6320; job_plan.rs:166) and a free-form dash bullet with no heading is not a named part.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part
rejected.why: Larger blast radius over fixtures the planner cannot run; false refusals on reworded bullets.

rejected.option: Only `N.`/`N)`/`(N)` parts, no bullets
rejected.why: Leaves out the acceptance bullets that criterion 3 and introspection 20261029-111141-1661 name.

rejected.option: Let a `N.` line after the heading count as both kinds
rejected.why: Double counting and two different needs for one line.

decisions.choice: 4. Stems (`part_stems`): strip a leading `[tag]` of a criterion; lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words; drop all-digit words and words under 3 letters. For each word w, let s = w without one trailing `s` when w is longer than 3. Drop the word when w OR s is in `FUNCTION_WORDS` (the, and, for, not, with, without, unless, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now), `COMMON_WORDS` (topics.rs:157-161) or `PART_FILLER` (pass, passes, passed, passing, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior). Otherwise keep s cut to 6 chars; then map the stem `doc` to `docume` (`STEM_ALIASES`). `stems_match(a, b)`: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other; 3-letter stems match exactly only. The unit test `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts the sets: (1) 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; (2) 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; (3) 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; criterion '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' = {docume, guide, descri, json}; and, for finding 4, 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' = {test, fail, change}, so 'passes' (bare word, singular 'passe') is dropped and the gate words of every generated request add no stems.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: the filler list was applied only to the singular stem, so 'passes' became 'passe' and was kept. Listing the inflected forms and testing both w and s closes it, and the pinned set shows it. COMMON_WORDS was written for `topic_words`, which keeps only 4+ letter words (topics.rs:165-177), so 'the', 'and' and 'for' need FUNCTION_WORDS or coverage would be almost free. The alias keeps 'docs/guide.md describes --json' covering '(2) Document the flag in the guide'.

rejected.option: Add only 'passe' to the filler list
rejected.why: Fixes one inflection; 'passed' and 'passing' would remain.

rejected.option: Keep 3-letter stems with 3-char prefix matching
rejected.why: 'the' or 'not' would match 'then', 'note'.

rejected.option: Drop the alias and require 4-letter stems
rejected.why: The natural criterion 'docs/guide.md describes --json' would share only 'guide' with part (2) and be falsely refused.

decisions.choice: 5. Coverage uses DISTINCTIVE stems. For each kind (Enumerated, Bullet) with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind; if that empties a part, fall back to its full stem set. Let n be the part's remaining stem count. A part is covered when (a) one usable criterion, pooled with the stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least `need` stems with the part, or (b) one deliverable path alone (split on non-alphanumerics) shares that many, or (c) a usable criterion cites the part's marker (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`) and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. need = min(2, n) for Enumerated parts and min(1, n) for Bullet parts. `out_of_scope` never covers. A part with n = 0 is skipped.
decisions.reason: Parts of one request share a subject: in the fixture 'flag' is in all three parts, so a criterion for part (2) such as 'the guide documents the flag' would share 'flag' with part (3). With 'flag' dropped, part (3) keeps {cover, timeou, test}, so that criterion cannot cover it. Bullets are reworded more often and nearly every steward, hestia and code_health request ends in an `Acceptance:` section (steward.rs:581-585; replay reads the newest 50 accepted readings, replay.rs:142-157), so bullets need one distinctive stem. The tension is named: a stricter matcher refuses more reworded readings, a looser one misses dropped parts; the replay holds a candidate whose newly refused share exceeds the declared 10% plus the 5-point margin, 15% (replay.rs:296-308). The 10% is an estimate because `records/` is absent.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to the one part it best matches
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules; dropping stems shared by all parts fixes the stated failure with one rule.

rejected.option: Hand-tune corpus wording until cases pass
rejected.why: Hides the sibling-subject gap; the fixture keeps 'flag' in all three parts on purpose and a unit test pins the stem sets.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: Summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: 6. Criterion-side negation, per part, in two lists, with the part's own vocabulary exempt. `DEFER_PHRASES` (job scope): follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. `CRITERION_NEGATION` = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of (work-state phrases). `MARKER_NEGATION` = CRITERION_NEGATION plus skipped, omitted, excluded, bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. For a part P, let the exempt phrases be those that appear in P's own text (by `has_phrase`, surveys.rs:39, lowercase). A criterion is unusable for P when it holds a CRITERION_NEGATION phrase that is not exempt, or when it cites P's marker and holds a MARKER_NEGATION phrase that is not exempt. A criterion unusable for P may still be usable for another part. `check_request_parts` records, for each uncovered part, every criterion that would have covered it but was unusable, with the phrase that caused it, and the error lists them ('criterion "..." was ignored because it holds "deferred"; reword it or cover the part with another criterion').
decisions.reason: Finding 1. skipped, omitted and excluded are everyday words for what this repository builds (skipped checks, excluded paths, omitted fields), so they cancel only a criterion that names the part's marker, where the writer is talking about the part itself. The other negation phrases say the work was not done, so 'The timeout test is deferred' still does not cover part (3). When the request's own part uses a phrase ('(2) Report skipped checks in status', '(3) Report deferred checks'), the criterion that echoes it is not cancelled, so the request's vocabulary never cancels its own criterion. The reader sees which criterion was ignored and why on the one re-read (reading.rs:738-759) and does not repeat it blindly. Bare 'later' stays out of CRITERION_NEGATION so 'Later retries reuse the cache' covers a part that it does not cite by marker. This job's own reading: its criteria that hold 'as a follow-up' or 'deferred' describe the test of a refusal; the request's three Acceptance bullets are covered by other criteria through one distinctive stem each, so none of them is lost.

rejected.option: Drop every work-state phrase and keep only job-scope phrases for criteria
rejected.why: 'The timeout test is deferred' would cover part (3); the on-the-re-read deferral by criterion would be open.

rejected.option: Keep the previous flat list (skipped, omitted, excluded cancel every criterion)
rejected.why: Refuses 'status lists skipped checks' for '(2) Report skipped checks in status'; finding 1.

rejected.option: Bare later and defer in the list for all criteria
rejected.why: Refuses good criteria such as 'Later retries reuse the cache' and '(3) Defer the flush until exit'.

decisions.choice: 7. The request defers a part only on a job-scope phrase: its own text, or another request sentence outside every part span and skipped line that holds a `DEFER_PHRASES` phrase and cites the marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N` (letters: `(c)`, `part c`, `item c`). Bare later, future, for now, separately, defer and out of scope do not defer a part of the request. Part spans are blanked before the request is split on newlines and '. '.
decisions.reason: Brief criterion 4: refuse 'unless the request text itself defers it'. Ordinary parts like '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately' and '(3) Defer the flush until exit' must stay required. A sentence 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.' is the request deferring. The list is a known limit; a deferral worded otherwise is refused and the error text gives the repair.

rejected.option: Check only the part's own text
rejected.why: Refuses a reading that follows a request deferring the part in a later sentence.

rejected.option: Broad list for request-side deferral
rejected.why: Exempts real parts.

decisions.choice: 8. Enforce by code only, and say in the doc comment and CHANGELOG why giving the reader information is not enough: the reader already sees the whole request and still deferred part (3) in jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, so the root-cause policy's allowance for a refusal rule (hestia.rs:1020-1022) applies. Name 'pass the parsed request parts to the reader in its brief' as a follow-up, not part of this job. No prompt is edited (reader budget 1998 of 2000, docs/system-facts.md).
decisions.reason: The refusal text reaches the reader on its corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759), which is the information channel that needs no new prompt tokens.

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt
rejected.why: No token headroom, and prose is not a mechanism.

rejected.option: Build the parsed parts into the reader brief now
rejected.why: A larger change across briefs and budgets; stated as a follow-up.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings that reword a part so it shares too few distinctive stems with any criterion. Stricter matching (needed to stop sibling parts covering each other) refuses more reworded readings; looser matching misses dropped parts.
risks.mitigation: The tension is named in the doc comment. Bullets need only one distinctive stem; parts with no stems are skipped; filler and gate words are filtered on both the word and its stem; a marker-citing criterion with one distinctive stem covers; one criterion pools with the paths it names; the error names the part, the repair and every ignored criterion, and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The proxy test over generated-request shapes guards the common case. The 10% is declared as an estimate; Athena's replay measures it at verification and the planner cannot (no `records/`).

risks.risk: A criterion that holds a work-state phrase (deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of) for a reason other than deferring the part, for example 'status lists deferred checks' for a part worded 'Report checks that wait', is ignored.
risks.mitigation: The phrase is exempt when the part's own text holds it; skipped, omitted and excluded cancel only criteria that cite the part's marker; the error lists the ignored criterion and the phrase, so the re-read can reword it. A known limit stated in the doc comment.

risks.risk: Dropping stems that occur in every part leaves a part with few stems, so a vague criterion covers it, or a part with n=0 is skipped.
risks.mitigation: If the drop empties a part, fall back to its full stem set; need = min(2, n). Skipping an all-shared part is a known limit stated in the doc comment; the corpus has a narrowed-part case.

risks.risk: An existing scripted or stored reading with an `Acceptance:` section or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the five listed files (reading.rs:7396, 7743; steward.rs:2585-2639; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only after an `Acceptance:` line and the search found no enumerated markers in requests outside the corpus. The producer runs `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test -p athena-core steward::tests`, `cargo test -p athena-core run::` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`, repairs the fixture's criteria, never the check, and names the file in the report.

risks.risk: Enumerations in quoted evidence of generated root-cause requests (title, 'Cause:', proposals), or a marker list in prose ('such as (1), (2) and (3)'), are read as parts.
risks.mitigation: Those lines are never parsed; an inline sequence counts only when every marker has text with a significant stem. Cases `request-parts-quoted-proposal-enumeration-ignored`, `request-parts-cause-title-enumeration-ignored` and `request-parts-marker-list-without-text` pin them.

risks.risk: The narrow request-side deferral list misses a real deferral worded another way, so a reading that follows the request is refused.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text says the request itself must defer the part; the re-read can cover it. A known limit in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The recorded request text of jobs sza7 and bw7k is not in the snapshot, so the corpus shapes are rebuilt from the introspections' account.
risks.mitigation: The case `source` strings say 'rebuilt from the introspection's account', not 'verbatim'; the unit tests hold the property for any part (3), not one job.

risks.risk: The producer tunes corpus wording until cases pass and hides a matcher gap.
risks.mitigation: Stem sets are pinned by `part_stems_worked_examples`; if a case's stem count differs from the plan, the producer reports it and fixes the rule or the case with the pinned set shown, and never lowers a threshold silently.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. Request: 'Do three things:' with '(1) Add the --json flag to status', '(2) Document the flag in the guide', '(3) Cover the flag with a timeout test', once inline and once as separate lines. All three parts name 'flag' on purpose. Base reading from `terms_reading` (reading.rs:7293, wraps `governed_reading` 4635) with deliverables src/status.rs and docs/guide.md and criteria '[behavior] status --json prints json' and '[content] docs/guide.md documents the flag'. (a) part 3 absent: `refuser_for(&reading, request)` (reading.rs:7288) returns `Some("check_request_parts")`; this also shows a criterion for part 2 does not cover part 3 through the shared 'flag'. (b) part 3 only in `out_of_scope` as a follow-up: same. (c) added criterion '[behavior] a test fails when the timeout is missing': `refuser_for` is None and `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok. (d) '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped: refused. (e) same reading with criterion 'Later retries reject future timestamps': accepted. (f) criterion 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' added to (a): still refused. (g) criterion 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later' added to (a): still refused. (h) criterion 'The timeout test is deferred' added to (a): still refused (finding 1, work-state phrase; part 3 text lacks 'deferred'). (i) request part '(2) Report skipped checks in status' with criterion 'status lists skipped checks': covered (finding 1, part's own vocabulary). (j) the same part with a criterion 'Part (2) skipped checks are omitted': ignored, and the error names the criterion and 'omitted'. `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts the stem sets of decision 4 including {test, fail, change} for the generated-request bullet and the distinctive sets after dropping 'flag'.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::request_parts_refused_when_part_three_is_left_out && cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::part_stems_worked_examples
demonstrations.observes: The refusing check is exactly `check_request_parts` for (a), (b), (d), (f), (g), (h); the reading is accepted for (c), (e), (i); the stem sets equal the stated ones.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `step!(check_request_parts(...))` line removed, `refuser_for` returns None for (a), (b), (d), (f), (g), (h) and the `Some("check_request_parts")` assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` through the existing helper `refuser_for` (reading.rs:7288); fixtures `terms_reading` and `governed_reading` exist. Nothing is faked and the check logic is not in the fixture. `part_stems` and `stems_match` are `pub(super)` in topics.rs so the test calls them directly. Tests added by plan step 5.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. On the part-three-moved-to-out_of_scope reading of criterion 2, `check_request_parts(..).unwrap_err().to_string()` contains the marker '(3)', 'timeout test', the cause 'out_of_scope' or 'follow-up', the repair 'deliverable and a criterion' and the exemption 'request itself defers'. With a criterion 'The timeout test is deferred' the error also contains 'was ignored because it holds "deferred"'. A request whose part reads '(3) Add a dashboard in a follow-up job', and a request with '(1)..(3)' followed by 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.', each with a reading that omits part 3: `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok. Parts '(3) Add a latest-value column', '(3) Reject future timestamps', '(3) Defer the flush until exit' and '(3) List each file separately' are NOT deferred: a reading that omits them is refused.
demonstrations.observes: The refusal names the part and the repair and every ignored criterion with its phrase; a job-scope deferral in the request, in the part or a later sentence, is accepted; words that merely resemble deferral do not defer.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `unwrap_err()` panics because the check is absent or returns Ok, so the first assertion fails.
